A draft or an edit names the version it is built on (baseVersion; null for a space's first draft), which must be the space's newest version that is not superseded — its draft when it has one, else its confirmed version; one built on another is refused WIKI_PLAN_STALE and nothing is written — unless it is a draft landing again under the idempotency key it was stored with (plan.idempotency). An acceptance is built on the newest version as it finds it, and is refused the same way when the plan moves while it is written.

idempotency.key: A draft may carry an idempotencyKey (at most 200 characters), the owner's as a changeset's is (refusalRules.idempotency): the version it stores keeps the key and the digest of its request — the request's JSON, keys sorted, with the space it names — and one key stores one version (UNIQUE (owner_id, idempotency_key)). An edit or an accepted proposal has none.
idempotency.replay: The same draft under the same key — the drafting job sends it again when the answer to its first send was lost on its way back — is answered with the version that key stored, replayed: true, before the plan is read and so before WIKI_PLAN_STALE: it writes nothing, publishes nothing and gates nothing, and the version is answered as it stands now. Two landings at once are one: under the space row's lock the second finds the first's version and is answered with it.
idempotency.reused: The same key with another request is refused WIKI_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (409) and nothing is written.
idempotency.answer: A draft's answer is the version, whole, with replayed: false when it was stored by this request and true when it is a replay.
idempotency.runner: The drafting job derives the key from its job and session and the draft it sends, so a draft sent again carries its key and another draft another; a draft under a key is sent again through a transient failure (wikiRecordsOnce), and one without is sent once.

gate.schema: Every field is one the schema has at its level (schema), or one declared as needing adding (newFields), of the right type and within rules; a section's kind is one of sectionKinds; category keys, document slugs and a document's section keys are unique.
gate.docCount: The plan has target.min to target.max documents: rules.docsMin to rules.docsMax unless the request names its own target.
gate.protected: A document the revised version protects is in the new version exactly as it was: the same slug, category and fields, and the same sections in the same order (their keys aside). Only the owner protects a document, so a draft or a proposal that protects one is refused. The owner's own edit is not checked: protecting is theirs.
gate.references: Every project a session condition names is one of the owner's (by id, or by an exact title only one project has), every topic a topic of the space, every entry kind one of the entry kinds; every document's category is one of the plan's categories, and every document a scope leaves something to (scopeOut[].docs) one of the plan's documents. A proposal's facts are an entry of the space or a session of the owner, or a commit named by its full sha (plan.proposals.factKindsNote).
gate.values: A message that names a value the request gave writes it as a JSON string — in double quotes, every character that would not show (a control or format character, a line or paragraph separator, a space other than U+0020) written as \uXXXX — so a backtick, an invisible character and a space at either end all show: on 10-01, «`decision` is no kind of entry: one of principle, convention, decision, …» read as decision refused for being decision, and the model wrote it the same way three rounds running. A closed-set value — a section's kind, a session condition's entryKinds and topics, a declared new field's at, a fact's kind — is read with the whitespace at either end and whatever backticks or quotes (` " ' “” ‘’ 「」 『』 «») wrap the whole of it taken off, as often as they do, a pair counting as a wrapping only with no more of either inside; nothing else is read loosely, so `decision` is the entry kind decision while Decision, decisions and decision with a zero-width space after it are none. The whitespace at the edge is the union of what the two paths trim — every Unicode space (U+0085 among them, which Go's TrimSpace takes off) and U+FEFF — so a value either side accepts is read here, and the runner's refusal of a BOM-wrapped value is not taken up (P10, 2026-10-08). The runner's own gate (plan.jobs.run) and a maintenance run's check of its proposal read and write values the same way.
gate.repo: Files, docs sections, symbols and contracts exist only in a checkout, which the server has none of: the drafting job checks them on the runner at a commit and reports repoCheck { sha, checked, missing: [{ kind, ref, at }] } with the draft (kind one of file, docSection, symbol, contract). The server keeps the report and its sha beside the version (repo_sha, repo_check) and does not judge it; a version the owner made carries none.
gate.errors: A request the gate refuses is WIKI_PLAN_GATE with errors[]: everything it found, each { check, path, message }, the path from the request's root (a draft's plan.docs[3].sections[2].sources.sessions.projects[0], an edit's doc. or section., a proposal's change.doc.) — and for what an edit or a proposal would make of the whole plan, from that plan's (plan.docs[20].protected) — the first rules.errorsMax listed. Nothing is stored, so the drafting job hands the list to the model and asks again.
gate.report: A version the gate let through keeps its report: { checkedAt, checks (each passed, or skipped for protected on an owner's edit), docs, target, needsNewFields: [{ at, name, why, values }] }.

proposals.means: Knowledge a maintenance run found that fits no section of the confirmed plan is a proposed change to it: why (reason), the document as it should read — one of the plan's by its slug, or a new one, with the category it opens when it needs one the plan does not have (change: { doc, category }) — and the facts that led to it (facts: [{ kind, id }]). It is gated against the confirmed version, protection included, and stored pending. It changes no version until the owner accepts it.

statuses.accepted: the owner accepted it: its document was applied to the plan's newest version and made a new draft (resultVersion) for the owner to confirm
statuses.rejected: the owner rejected it; the plan is as it was

proposals.factKindsNote: A fact is an entry of the space, a session of the owner, or — for a design document that landed on origin/main and that no section cites — the commit that added it, named by its full sha (40 hex characters). The server has no checkout: it holds a commit to its shape, and the maintenance run found it on origin/main.
proposals.accept: Applies the document to the plan's newest version — in place of the document of its slug, or after the last document of its category — and gates the result again, protection included, since the plan may have moved since it was proposed: a result the gate refuses is WIKI_PLAN_GATE and the proposal stays pending. Otherwise the new draft and the proposal's settling are one transaction.
proposals.reject: Settles the proposal, with the owner's note if there is one; no version changes.
proposals.author: Who filed it (migration 0407): a maintenance session (author_session_id), or the server's maintenance run (author_job_id) when the wiki worker proposed it — exactly one, held by wiki_plan_proposal_author_chk. An owner's decision on the proposal is neither: decided_by_user_id is on the row beside them.

plan.guard: requireConfirmedPlan(db, { ownerId, spaceId }) in src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-plan.ts: the space's confirmed version ({ id, version, confirmedAt }), or WIKI_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED. Every writer of a space's documents calls it before it writes one, so no document is written from a plan the owner did not confirm; a maintenance run's proposal needs it too.

who.draft: A Wiki maintenance run of the space (isWikiMaintenanceSession, maintenance.session), through the runner door: its drafting job's draft, its read of the plan, and its proposals. Any other session is refused WIKI_NOT_MAINTENANCE_SESSION, a headless call 400, and another owner's space is a plain 404.
who.owner: The owner, through the user door and only there: every read of the plan, an edit, a confirmation, an acceptance or a rejection. A request with a session header is refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY before anything is read, whatever the session's role; the runner door has no route that confirms or decides anything. Another owner's space, version or proposal is a plain 404.

reads.state: { spaceId, confirmed, draft, proposals, job }: the version in force and the draft, each whole or null, the pending proposals, oldest first, and the space's plan job (plan.jobs.read), or null when it never had one.
reads.versions: Every version, newest first: { id, version, status, origin, baseVersion, proposalId, docCount, createdAt, confirmedAt, supersededAt }.
reads.version: One version whole: its status, origin, baseVersion, categories, newFields, target, gate report, repoCheck, model, who made and confirmed it and when, and its documents in order, each with its sections in order; a session condition's projects are { id, title } with the title as it stands now (null for a project since deleted).

requests.draft: { baseVersion, target?, plan: { categories, docs, newFields? }, repoCheck, model?, idempotencyKey? }
requests.edit: { baseVersion, docSlug, doc } for a whole document (a new slug renames it), or { baseVersion, docSlug, sectionKey, section } for one of its sections
requests.propose: { reason, change: { doc, category? }, facts: [{ kind, id }] }
requests.redraft: { instructions? }: with instructions (at most plan.jobs.rules.instructionsMaxChars characters) a revision, without them a draft

plan.view: Not knowledge: no source kind names a plan, so citing one is WIKI_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED; the push and the agent's search and get read entries alone.
plan.tool: none: no MCP tool reads, confirms or decides anything of the plan (hard constraint 2). The drafting job's verbs are the CLI's.

jobs.means: A space's plan is drafted, revised and built by jobs the server runs as tasks of the space's hidden Wiki maintenance list (maintenance.list), so the session that runs one is a maintenance session (isWikiMaintenanceSession) and the plan's runner door is open to it and to nothing else. A fact asks for a job — the space's creation, or its owner — never a clock.

kinds.draft: orbit wiki plan draft: a whole plan drafted from the repository at origin/main and what the space already knows, keeping every document the version it revises protects
kinds.revise: orbit wiki plan revise: the space's newest version revised with the owner's instructions; a space with no version yet is drafted with the instructions as the owner's guidance
kinds.build: orbit wiki docs build: the documents of a confirmed version written section by section, which the owner's confirmation asks for; a section whose material did not change since it was written is left as it is, so after a small change only what changed is written again

triggers.space_created: the space was created: through POST /api/wiki/spaces, or on the first proposal of a session whose workspace's repository had no space yet
triggers.owner: the owner asked on the plan page: for a draft or a revision, POST /api/wiki/spaces/:id/plan/redraft; for a build, by confirming a version, POST /api/wiki/spaces/:id/plan/versions/:version/confirm

states.queued: the space's maintenance list has a task that has not ended; the job is made when a task of the owner's ends, before the next maintenance run (staggered)
states.held: the space's maintenance names no workspace, or a provider no run could start on (held.reason); the job is made when the owner's next change to the maintenance settings, or their next request, finds that settled
states.running: its task is made: dispatched, or running, with the gate round it is on — a build with how far it has got (progress)
states.succeeded: its run stored a draft the gate let through (version); a build's wrote the documents of a confirmed version (version) and left no section unwritten
states.failed: its run ended without one — errors are the gate's on its last round — or its task ended before the run said how it went

held.where: wiki_plan_job.held_reason and held_at, served as the job's held: { reason, at }, or null. Written when a job is not made for one of the reasons, keeping the time the reason first held, as maintenance.job.held is on the cursor; cleared when its task is made.
held.no_maintenance_workspace: settings.maintenance.workspaceId names no workspace of the owner's: a draft runs where maintenance runs.
held.maintenance_provider_unusable: settings.maintenance.provider is one no maintenance run could start on (wikiMaintenanceProviderProblem): missing, turned off, or not on the Claude Code runtime.

jobs.request: A request asks for a draft, or with instructions a revision. The space's draft or revision that has not ended answers it (one open a space, a partial unique index) and is asked again whether it may be made now; a made job whose task already ended, or is gone, without its run saying how is ended failed first, so it cannot stand in the way. Otherwise a job is recorded and asked at once: held when the settings say so; queued when the list has a task that has not ended; else made. A build is asked for by the owner's confirmation of a version, after it commits and never failing it: the space's build that waits (queued or held, one a space, a partial unique index) answers it, pointed at the newer version, and is asked again; a build already made does not stand in the way — it writes the version it was made for, and the waiting one the next, behind its task. A build names its version from the start (version), and keeps it when it fails.
jobs.trigger: WikiPlanJobFacts takes every task change this replica publishes (task.changed), whether published for the owner or on a session: the runner's doors publish the change of a task a session's turn or end settled on that session, read for the session's owner — which is how a maintenance run's task ends, its acceptance turn's comparison settling it. The made jobs of the tasks it names are ended failed when their task ended before the run said how it went, and the owner's queued jobs are asked again, since the list may have just been freed. The maintenance trigger asks a space's queued jobs again too, when a fact finds its list free (staggered). The owner's change to a space's maintenance settings asks its queued and held jobs again. No clock asks anything.
jobs.staggered: A job and the space's maintenance runs share its list, one task at a time, and a queued job goes first: the maintenance trigger makes no task while the list has one that has not ended, nor while a job of the space is queued (maintenance.job.trigger.notMade) — a fact that finds the list free makes the job's task instead — so when a maintenance run's task ends the job's task is made before any next run, and the facts that arrived meanwhile wait in the backlog for the first fact after the job's task ended. A job waits behind a run the same way, so the local model is never asked by both at once. A held job waits for the owner's settings, not for the list, and stands in no run's way.
jobs.notAMaintenanceRun: A job's task is not a maintenance run: it is not counted against settings.maintenance.dailyRunLimit (wikiMaintenanceRunsToday counts the list's other tasks), the day's limit does not hold it back, and it runs whether or not maintenance is turned on — the list is made for it when the space has none, and the claim does not refuse its session for maintenance being off (maintenance.run).

task.list: the space's hidden Wiki maintenance list (maintenance.list), made for the job when the space has none
task.title: Wiki plan draft: <space title>, Wiki plan redraft: <space title> for a revision, or Wiki documents: <space title> for a build
task.provider: settings.maintenance.provider, pinned: the session is claimed as maintenance.run says
task.runAt: the moment it is made: the dispatcher's next scan starts it
task.creator: USER, the space's owner
task.description: the run's instructions: run `orbit wiki plan draft --space <id>` (or `revise`) once, and report the documents, the gate rounds with their errors, the token spend and the time it printed; a revision's instructions are quoted below them. A build's: run `orbit wiki docs build --space <id>` once, and report the documents and sections written, unchanged and failed, the token spend and the time. Either way its Bash call is given timeout maintenance.run.bashTimeoutMs, and a call the tool cut off before the command ended is not run again (maintenance.run.bashCall)

jobs.read: The plan's read (plan.reads.state) carries the space's job that has not ended, else the one that ended last: { id, spaceId, kind, trigger, state, instructions, requestedAt, held, waitingFor: { taskId, title, sessionId, startedAt } for a queued one, taskId, provider, sessionId, madeAt, startedAt, endedAt, attempt, attemptsMax, progress, version, errors, error, report, draft } — draft being the last draft of a failed job, as its run sent it to the gate, and progress a build's { docs: { done, total }, current: { slug, title } | null }, null for a draft.

who.redraft: The owner, on the owner channel only: a request with a session header is refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY before anything is read. Its answer is { created, job }: the job made, or the space's draft that had not ended.
who.runner: context, progress, finish and materials are a maintenance run's of the space alone, as the plan's other runner routes are: any other session WIKI_NOT_MAINTENANCE_SESSION, a headless call 400, another owner's space a plain 404. context, progress and finish answer a maintenance run whose task no job was made for WIKI_PLAN_NO_JOB, and progress a job that has ended the same way, as finish does any end but the one the job ended with. check answers the space's owner's runner with no session too — a task's acceptance command runs with none.

jobs.context: { job, space: { id, title, repo: { urlNorm, rootCommitSha }, workspace: { id, workDir } } }: the job the calling session's task was made for and where its run starts; records the session and the time it first started.
jobs.progress: { attempt }: the gate round a draft's or a revision's run is on, 1 to rules.attemptsMax; a build's { docs: { done, total }, current: { slug, title } | null }: the documents of the confirmed version it went through, and the one it writes now — what the plan page shows while it runs.
jobs.finish: { outcome: succeeded | failed, version?, errors?, error?, report?, draft?, attempt? }: a run that succeeded names the version its draft became, a draft of the space this very session stored; one that failed carries the gate's errors on its last round (at most plan.rules.errorsMax), what went wrong in words (redacted, at most rules.errorMaxChars), and the last draft it had (at most rules.draftMaxBytes of JSON). The report is at most rules.reportMaxBytes of JSON. A build that succeeded names the confirmed version it wrote, one the owner confirmed; one that failed keeps the version it was made for, and its report is WikiPlanBuildReport (buildReport). The job is ended with it, once: the same end said again by the run that said it (the runner sends it again when the answer to its first send was lost) is answered with what was kept and changes nothing; any other end is refused WIKI_PLAN_NO_JOB.

check.passes: The job ended succeeded, and the version it names is one of the space's — for a build, one its owner confirmed.
check.exit: 0 when it passes; 1 otherwise, with each reason a sentence: the run did not say how it ended, it failed (with its error and how many errors the gate's last round found), or the version it names is missing.

jobs.materials: { spaceId, title, asOf, repo, workspace, projects: [{ id, title, status, createdAt, tasks, sessions }], sessions: { days, total, items: [{ title, month, task, project, provider }] }, entries: [{ kind, status, count }], topics: [{ slug, title, category, pathPrefixes, active, recent: [{ kind, title }] }] }: the owner's projects (at most rules.materialsProjectsMax, oldest first), the sessions of the space's workspaces of the last rules.materialsSessionDays days (at most rules.materialsSessionsMax, newest first, with the total), and how the space's entries and topics are spread. Every title is redacted before it leaves the server; the runner counts and clusters.
jobs.report: What a run reports when it ends (WikiPlanJobReport): categories, docs, sections, target, attempts [{ attempt, local, server, checks }] — each gate round's errors found by the runner's own gate and by the server's, by check — repo { sha, checked, missing }, tokens { input, output, calls }, seconds, model, and rulesDraft: the fourth step's draft of the rules, cut to fit.
jobs.buildReport: What a build's run reports when it ends (WikiPlanBuildReport): planVersion, repoSha, docs { total, written }, sections { written, unchanged, failed }, tokens { input, output, calls }, seconds, model.

steps: context: GET …/plan/job — the job, the space, its repository and the maintenance workspace's checkout; and GET …/plan — the version it revises and the documents that version protects
checkout: the maintenance workspace's work directory, ~ expanded to the runner account's home, fetched; a checkout that is not the space's repository fails the run

materials: the repository at origin/main — its modules and entry points, the docs heading tree (docs/mocks and docs/evidence left out), the contracts and the code's symbols — and GET …/plan/materials, the owner's projects, the space's sessions counted and clustered by title, and its entries and topics

draft, in four steps each streamed to disk as it is written: the catalogue's skeleton (categories and documents), each category's documents in detail, each document's outline with where every section's material comes from, and a draft of the rules; one clean Claude Code call to the local model a unit, in a compact line format

gate: the runner's own gate first — schema, docCount, protected, references (files, docs sections, symbols and contracts at the sha, every project and topic, and every → x.y or 见 x.y a document of the plan) and, for a revision, sections moved out only of kind conventions — then the server's (POST …/plan/drafts)
redo: whatever either gate found is handed back to the model, unit by unit, and the draft gated again: rules.attemptsMax rounds in all
finish: POST …/plan/job/finish with the version the draft became, or the last round's errors
run.revise: A revision asks the model for the new catalogue — each document with the documents of the version it revises that it is made from, and the sections it moves into a category for agents — then writes again only the documents that merge or are new; one made from a single document of the version keeps its outline, less the sections moved out. The documents it hands the model, and a document a redo hands back, name their session conditions' projects by title, as every drafting prompt names a project, and never by an id the model would have to copy; a project keeps its id only where its title is one another project shares, or the materials' list of projects may have been cut. A protected document is carried as it is, and a move out of one, or of a section of any kind but conventions, is refused by the runner's gate.
run.model: Every call is a clean Claude Code (agentSurface.verify.cleanClaudeCode) on the model this session's provider names, thinking off, its answer streamed to a file as it arrives; the run waits for the endpoint's /health before its first call and stops at the first 401.
run.build: A build's run is orbit wiki docs build in the job's session: GET …/plan/job first — which records it started — then every document of the confirmed version, section by section (docs.build), POST …/plan/job/progress as each document is taken up, and POST …/plan/job/finish with the version it wrote and its report: succeeded when no section was left unwritten, failed with why otherwise.

cli.draft: orbit wiki plan draft --space <id> [--target MIN-MAX] [--model MODEL] [--concurrency N] [--work-dir DIR] [--json]
cli.revise: orbit wiki plan revise --space <id> [--instructions <file>] [--target MIN-MAX] [--model MODEL] [--concurrency N] [--work-dir DIR] [--json]
cli.build: orbit wiki docs build --space <id> [--json] (docs.build.cli), run in the build's session
cli.tool: none: all three are CLI only. draft and revise are the plan job's run alone, and check is its task's acceptance command, which runs where there is no session.
cli.draftPrecondition: Run this only as the plan job of the space, once, and let it finish: it drafts as the space's maintenance run, and only a draft that passed the plan's gate is stored — three rounds at most, each handing every error back to the model.
cli.revisePrecondition: Run this only as the plan job the owner's redraft made, once, and let it finish: it revises the plan's newest version with the owner's instructions, and only a draft that passed the plan's gate is stored — three rounds at most, each handing every error back to the model.
cli.checkPrecondition: Judge a plan job only by what this reads: it passes when the job's run stored a draft that passed the plan's gate — or, a build's, wrote the documents of the confirmed version it was made for — and a run cannot pass it by saying it finished.

server.why: The plan's model moves off the runner (design section 0): when the executor switch gives the account to the server, a draft or a revision is a wiki_job the wiki-worker runs with the System model — the runner's pipeline (src/runner-go/wiki_plan_*.go) ported to src/apiserver/src/wiki-worker/wiki-plan-*.ts, its repository read from the space's snapshot — and no task, session or provider of the account's is made or spent.
server.when: Under jobs.executor=server, or canary for an account its list names. Under runner (the default), and for an account canary does not list, a job is made as plan.jobs.task says and run as plan.jobs.run says, exactly as before.
server.make: advanceWikiPlanJob asks the switch first: a draft is made as a `plan_draft` wiki_job and a revision as `plan_revise`, at priority, with input { planJobId }, in the transaction that marks the plan job made with it (wiki_plan_job.job_id). The space's maintenance workspace is still what it needs — the worker reads the repository through that workspace's runner — so a space without one is held no_maintenance_workspace as on the runner's path; the provider is not asked, since no session's model is, and nothing waits for the hidden list (plan.jobs.staggered is the runner's: the queue and one running job a space keep the model from being asked by both at once). No task is made.
server.build: A build is made as a `docs_build` wiki_job on the same path (P7, docs.build.server): by advanceWikiPlanJob, at docs.build.server.priority with input { planJobId }, in the transaction that marks the plan job made with it — held no_maintenance_workspace without a workspace, the provider not asked and nothing waiting for the hidden list, as a draft. Its run says how far it got on the plan job ({ docs, current }, as plan.jobs.progress says a build's run does) and ends it as plan.jobs.finish does a build's — the version it wrote, the build's report — with no session (docs.build.server.progress, docs.build.server.end). A build made before the switch, a task, ends with its task: its session is refused like any other (door).
server.priorityRule: Owner-initiated (jobs.priority): the space's creation and the owner's redraft are both the owner's, so every request of the job goes before background maintenance.
server.systemPrompt: 你是这个仓库的文档主编。你根据给你的材料规划产品与技术文档。只使用材料里出现的文件路径、章节标题、符号、项目名，不编造。用中文写，代码名、路径、命令保留原文。只输出要求的内容。
server.calls: Every call is one queue request (modelQueue): step one of steps — each `plan_*`, so it waits at most modelQueue.waitLimitSeconds.plan and runs at most modelQueue.callBudgetSeconds.plan, sixty minutes — and unit `a<round>/<the runner's unit name>@<the first 12 hex of the call's sha256>`, so a replay meets the request it already made, an answer that does not read is asked again with the format said once more (formatTries calls a unit at most), and a changed question is a new request. maxTokens a call, the system prompt above, one user message; what has arrived is kept as the request's partial while it runs (modelQueue).
server.materials: Read once, at the job's first run, and kept on the plan job (wiki_plan_job.materials, migration 0404): the space's snapshot's sha — a fresh snapshot when its runner can take one, waited for at most snapshotWaitSeconds, else the snapshot the space holds, else the job waits as infra — the plan's materials (plan.jobs.materials, the same function the runner door answers with), the day they were read, and the texts at the sha the snapshot does not carry: the overview's documents and schema.prisma, through the runner's read (repoOps.kinds.read), waited for at most readWaitSeconds. A replay reads them back, so it asks the model the questions it asked; a snapshot that moved under the job (another job of the space took a newer one) makes it start over at the snapshot as it is, as the runner starts over when the sha it drafted from left origin/main.
server.materialCapsRule: The runner's caps, in characters: a catalogue reads the overview at full, the structure and the documents' heading tree at full; a category's details read them at detail; a document's outline reads the overview at doc and its code's symbols within codeExcerpt (bytes, as the runner's builder counts them).
server.repository: Everything the runner's job read of its checkout is read from the snapshot index at the same sha: the files with their sizes (the structure, hasPath), every document's headings (the heading trees, hasDocSection), every source file's symbols (the code excerpt, hasSymbol), the contracts' top-level keys (the contracts list). A symbol the index does not name is looked for, as on the runner, as a word of its file's text — the whole text of the file, read at the sha before the round is gated (repoOps.kinds.read). The index carrying an object's keys only (a contract whose JSON is an array or empty reads as not JSON) is the one place the two paths can still differ.
server.gate: The job's own gate first — plan.jobs.run's checks, word for word, with every file, docs section, symbol and contract checked on the snapshot — then the plan's gate on the server (plan.gate), which the job reaches in process (WikiPlans.submitServerDraft) under the draft's idempotency key; repoCheck is the snapshot's sha and what this gate found. Whatever either finds goes back to the model unit by unit, plan.jobs.rules.attemptsMax rounds in all.
server.author: A stored version names the wiki_job that drafted it (wiki_plan.author_job_id, migration 0404; authorJobId on the read) where a session's names its session; origin maintenance, model the System model's name.
server.progress: The plan job says where the run is, as plan.jobs.progress does for a session's: started_at at the job's first run, attempt at each round — what the plan page reads. The wiki_job's own progress (jobs.progress) is { planJobId, attempt, step }.
server.finish: The run ends its plan job as plan.jobs.finish does a session's, held to the same rules (WikiPlans.finishServerJob): succeeded with the version its draft became — a version of the space this wiki_job stored — or failed with the last round's errors, what went wrong, the report and the last draft; the wiki_job ends with { kind, planJobId, outcome, version, error, plan: the report }. A failure of the platform — a request past its wait limit, the space's runner away, the worker stopping — is not the draft's: the wiki_job is retried (jobs.retry) and the plan job stays running. A wiki_job that ends without its plan job ended ends it failed, and one that never started is cancelled, with its plan job ended, when the switch no longer gives the account to the server.
server.door: The runner door's drafting routes are the server's (refusals: WIKI_SERVER_EXECUTES), whoever asks, once the space is found: context, progress, finish, materials and drafts — a build job's session too, since the documents are the server's as well (build): no build task is made, and one made before the switch stops at its first call like any other session. A session's `orbit wiki plan draft` or `revise` — one that predates this too — stops at its first call, before it has asked any model anything. What a maintenance run reads of the plan (plan.reads.state) and proposes to it (plan.proposals), and the check (plan.jobs.check), are as they were. Under runner every route is exactly as plan.jobs.who says.
server.deterministic: One fixture holds both paths to the same answers: src/shared/src/wiki-plan.fixture.json, written by src/runner-go/wiki_plan_fixture_test.go from a real checkout read the runner's way, and read by src/apiserver/src/wiki-worker/wiki-plan-golden.spec.ts the server's way — the line format read back, the references found, the materials, every step's prompt, each round's draft, gate errors and repository check.

docs.means: A space's documents, written section by section from the plan its owner confirmed (plan.guard): a document is a plan document, named by its slug, and a section a plan section, named by its key. Every footnote points at a first-hand original — a design-document section, code or a contract at a commit, or one of Orbit's own records — with its verbatim quote, and the entry it was found through is kept as the via entry: an entry is the way in, never the source. What each sentence is, and how each footnote was checked, is stored sentence by sentence. A document is a view for people: never pushed, never a source, and never returned by wiki_search or wiki_get. The topic articles (articles, wiki_topic_summary) stay, readable as they are, until the clients have moved to the documents.

statuses.ok: no more than rules.needsReviewAbove of its sentences are unsourced or unverified
statuses.needs_review: more than rules.needsReviewAbove of its sentences are unsourced or unverified: the whole document is marked for review

sentenceStatuses.sourced: it carries a footnote whose check passed (verdict verified)
sentenceStatuses.transition: it carries no footnote and brings no new fact: every fact token in it (factTokens) is already in a sourced sentence or a heading of the same document
sentenceStatuses.unsourced: it carries no footnote and states a fact no sourced sentence or heading of the document carries; the tokens that are new are stored with it
sentenceStatuses.unverified: it carries footnotes, and none of them passed its check
sentenceStatuses.withdrawn: a footnote of it came through an entry since rejected, retired or superseded, or whose anchor changed or went missing, or cites a repository file deleted or renamed on origin/main (withdrawal); it stays, struck through, until its section is written again

footnoteKinds.design_doc: a section of a design document in the repository: path@sha#Lstart-end, and the section's heading
footnoteKinds.code: code in the repository: path@sha#Lstart-end, and the symbol
footnoteKinds.contract: a contract in the repository: path@sha#Lstart-end
footnoteKinds.turn: a conversation turn, by its id
footnoteKinds.event: a run event — a reply, a thinking, a tool call's input or its result, an error — by its id
footnoteKinds.tool_call: a tool call's output, by its id
footnoteKinds.task: a task's title and description, by its id
footnoteKinds.task_comment: a task comment, by its id
footnoteKinds.approval: an approval's answers and note, by its id
footnoteKinds.owner_decision: a blocker the owner resolved with a note, by its id
footnoteKinds.merge_receipt: a merge receipt, by its id
footnoteKinds.note: a file orbit wiki import registered, by its id

verdicts.verified: the quote is in the original
verdicts.not_found: the quote is not in the original; a quote shorter than rules.quoteMinChars once folded is not checked, and is not found either
verdicts.no_quote: the footnote gave no quote, so nothing could be checked
verdicts.unresolved: the record it names is not one of this account's — another owner's, deleted, or none at all; a repository footnote is never unresolved

checkers.server: a record's footnote: the server read the record again and checked the quote itself
checkers.runner: a repository footnote: the runner checked the quote at sha, in the checkout the server does not have

blockKinds.item: a list item, cut into sentences
blockKinds.heading: a heading inside the section: its text, which counts as a heading for factTokens
blockKinds.code: a fenced code block: its text, which is not checked

docs.rulesNote: Lengths are counted in characters (Unicode code points). needsReviewAbove is a share of all the document's sentences, withdrawn ones included: more than it marks the whole document, and exactly 5% does not. quoteMinChars counts the folded quote (verification.normalization). sectionsPerWrite is plan.rules.sectionsMax, so one write can carry a whole document. errorsMax is the most errors one refusal lists; its message counts them all. dispositionsPerSection is the most pieces of material one section's ledger lists (dispositions), and reasonMaxChars the longest reason one of them gives.
docs.schemaNote: Every field a write may carry, at each level, and no other: anything else is refused WIKI_DOC_INVALID. planVersion, repoSha (the origin/main commit the run read the repository at, 40 lowercase hex) and sections are required; model is not. A section needs key (a section of the confirmed plan's document, once per write), materialSha256 (64 lowercase hex), markdown (not blank, at most rules.markdownMaxChars) and footnotes (at most rules.footnotesPerSection, and may be empty). A repository footnote (repoKinds) needs path, sha (7-64 lowercase hex: one with no sha is refused), lines { start, end } (1-based, inclusive) and verified, the runner's own check; section, symbol, quote, excerpt and viaEntryId are optional. A record footnote (recordKinds) needs ref, the record's id; chars { start, end } (code points of the record's redacted text, end exclusive), quote and viaEntryId are optional. viaEntryId, when given, is an entry of the space. A quote is at most rules.quoteMaxChars; null or left out is no quote. A section's dispositions (optional; at most rules.dispositionsPerSection) are its material's ledger (dispositions): each names the material by the id the runner gave it (material, at most 16 characters), its kind (a repoKind or a recordKind), where it is (ref: a repository path with its lines, path#Lstart-end, or a record's id), what became of it (action, one of dispositionActions), the material it was merged into (into: required for merge, null otherwise) and why (reason, not blank, at most rules.reasonMaxChars).

dispositionActions.adopt: the model's merge adopted it: it was handed to the writer
dispositionActions.merge: the model's merge folded it into another piece of the same section (into), which says the same thing with more weight or later; it was handed to the writer beside it
dispositionActions.drop: the model's merge dropped it — superseded, off the section's subject, or a guess — and the writer never saw it
dispositionActions.over_cap: the runner never handed it to the model: the section's material was full (build.rules.materialMaxChars) before its turn came
dispositionActions.filtered: the runner took it out by rule before the model saw it: a platform-generated template message (build.templates), or the same text as another piece of the section

docs.dispositions: What became of each piece of a section's material, kept with the section it explains (wiki_doc_section.dispositions, dispositionsMigration): the merge's word for every piece it was handed — adopt, merge into another, or drop, each with its reason — and the runner's for the pieces it never handed over (over_cap, filtered). A write stores the ledger as it came, beside the section it replaces; the ledger of a section left unchanged is left as it was. The reads return it with each section (reads.doc, reads.writerDoc).
docs.markdown: A section's body is Markdown with footnote markers [n], n naming its section's footnotes[n-1]. A first line that is a heading is the section's own title, which the plan names, and is dropped. A fenced code block is one code block and is not checked; any other heading line is a heading block; a list item (-, *, +, 1., 1), 1、) is an item block, and an indented line under it continues it; other lines up to a blank line are one paragraph (a leading > is dropped, a line of three dashes, stars or underscores is skipped). Paragraphs and items are cut into sentences as articles.validation.sentences cuts an article — at 。！？, and at a full stop or an ASCII ? or ! before a space or the line's end, outside code spans — so a ； ends nothing. A marker outside a code span names a footnote; one outside 1 to the section's footnote count names none and is dropped (stats.markersDropped), and a run of markers with no words is not a sentence. A section with no sentence is refused.

verification.records: The server reads the record again, among the account's own rows, through the one reader a record has (WikiService.sourceText, whose texts wiki-verify-evidence.ts defines: runEventText for an event, a tool call's name, input and output together, an approval's answers and note — and the plan it decided — a merge receipt's and an owner decision's line as the dossier writes them), so a document and an entry citing the same record check their quotes against the same words; it redacts it with the shared redactor and the owner's workspace.env values, and looks for the quote — redacted the same way — in it, both folded (normalization). chars, when given, narrows the search to that range. The range the quote was found at is stored (char_start, char_end: code points of the redacted text), and so are the record's session, number, time and label, for the page's link. A translated, paraphrased or spliced quote — two passages of the record joined as one — is not found.
verification.repository: The server has no checkout. A repository footnote carries the runner's own check of its quote against the lines it names (verified) and the commit it read them at (sha); it is stored as checked by the runner at that sha, and a footnote with no sha is refused. excerpt, when the runner sends it, is those lines as it read them, redacted, for the page to show.
verification.normalization: Before a quote is compared, quote and original alike are folded: Unicode NFC; the full-width punctuation ，。：；（）！？「」“”‘’、『』【】—– read as its ASCII counterpart; ** and __ and backticks dropped; a Markdown escape read as the character it escapes; every whitespace dropped. The original is compared a second time with each line's leading comment marker (//, ///, /*, *, */ or #) taken off, so a quote of a comment's words is found. A quote is one passage: an ellipsis is not a gap to skip.

docs.factTokens: A sentence's fact tokens: each code span (its content); each ASCII identifier or path ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_./-]*[A-Za-z0-9_]) of at least 3 characters that is not one of the, and, for, with, not, are, can, its, but, via; each number of two or more digits; and each number with a unit (秒 分钟 小时 天 个 条 次 % ms s MB KB) — matched in that order, lowercased, whitespace dropped.
docs.classification: A sentence with a footnote is sourced when one of its footnotes is verified and unverified when none is; withdrawn when one of them came through an entry withdrawal names. A sentence with none is a transition when every fact token in it is among those of the document's sourced sentences and headings — its plan sections' titles, the heading blocks of its written sections, its title and its question — and unsourced otherwise, its new tokens stored with it. The whole document is classified again each time a section of it is written, so a transition answers to what the other sections say now. The document is needs_review when its unsourced and unverified sentences are more than rules.needsReviewAbove of all of them; withdrawn sentences are not counted among those: they wait for their section to be written again.
docs.fingerprint: materialSha256 is the runner's: sha256 over the section's definition in the plan (title, kind, covers, length, sources) and the material it gathered for it, as it gathered it. An overview's material is its document's other sections: its fingerprint is taken over its definition and theirs, so it is written again whenever one of them is. The repository's commit is not in it — only what was read at it — so a commit that changed nothing a section cites leaves the section as it is. The server does not recompute it; it compares it with the one stored.
docs.repoSha: Every section is stored with the origin/main commit it was generated at (repoSha, from the write that wrote it), and a document with its last write's. A maintenance run compares a section's repoSha with origin/main as it stands, and writes again a section whose design documents, code or contracts changed since (owner 2026-09-29: the wiki follows what agents write into docs/); that comparison is the run's, and the server only keeps the sha and hands it back (reads.writerState, reads.doc).
docs.regeneration: A section whose stored materialSha256 is the one a write names, and from which nothing was withdrawn (stale_at null), is not written again: its outcome is unchanged and its rows are left as they are. Every other section a write names is replaced whole, its sentences and footnotes with it. A write names the confirmed plan version it was written from (planVersion); one that is not the confirmed version is WIKI_PLAN_STALE and writes nothing. A section the confirmed plan's document no longer has is dropped when the document is next written. No clock rewrites anything (hard constraint 5): the maintenance run writes after facts arrived.
docs.withdrawal: When an entry is rejected, retired or superseded, or its anchor state becomes changed or missing, every sentence with a footnote that came through it (via entry) is withdrawn — status withdrawn, with when, why (withdrawReasons) and the entry — and its section is marked stale (stale_at), so the next maintenance run writes it again. It happens in the entry's own transaction, at its single state writer (WikiService.recomputeFlags, which every applyOp branch ends in; storage.singleWriter), so no path that moves an entry can forget it. A write with a footnote that comes through such an entry stores that sentence withdrawn, and its section stale, at once; and it takes its via entries FOR SHARE before anything else, so a rejection racing it waits for it and then withdraws what it wrote.
docs.withdrawalPaths: A repository file a section's footnotes cite that a maintenance run found deleted or renamed on origin/main (maintenance.job.docs.byRepo) withdraws every sentence of the space's documents with a footnote citing it — status withdrawn, anchor_missing, with when and the path (withdrawn_path) in place of an entry — and marks its section stale (routes.withdraw). A sentence names the entry or the path that withdrew it, one of the two (migration 0340's CHECK). The documents are taken in id order as a write and an entry's withdrawal take them.

affected.means: What a maintenance run writes again because of the entries, and what it may propose (reads.affected): the server's half of maintenance.job.docs. The repository's half is the run's, in its checkout.
affected.fit: An entry fits a section's session condition when a keyword is in its title, summary, fields or aliases, one of its anchors' paths is under one of anchorPaths, or — when it is of one of entryKinds, or the condition names none — one of its topics is one of topics, or one of its live sources is a record of a session or a task of one of projects (a session of one of the project's tasks, or its coordinator's; the task, or a comment on it). It scores 3 a keyword, 2 a path, 1 a topic, 1 a kind, 1 a project. material.entries picks a section's entries by the same rule.
affected.sections: A written section of the confirmed plan is written again when an entry that fits it had an op applied to it after the section was generated, or when it is stale.
affected.unplaced: An entry an op applied to since the space's first plan version was made, live and with its anchors standing, that fits no section of the confirmed plan and that no proposal of the space names, whatever became of the proposal — newest first, at most rules.unplacedMax, unplacedMore counting the rest.

links.sessionRecord: A footnote on a turn, an event or a tool call carries the record's id (recordId) and the session it is in (sessionId), both read when the write checked it: wiki_source keeps a record's id alone, and the page needs the pair to link the record — web sessionRecordHref(sessionId, recordId), iOS SessionRecordLink.url(session:record:), which open the session at it through GET /api/sessions/:id/events/page?around=<recordId>. Any other record carries what it is in: an approval or a merge receipt its session (sessionId), a task comment its task (taskId), an owner decision its project (projectId), a note its path (notePath).
links.repository: A repository footnote carries its path, sha and lines (path@sha#Lstart-end): the page links that file at that commit in the space's repository.

view.push: Never in <orbit_wiki_context>: the push reads wiki_entry and nothing else.
view.source: Never a source: no source kind names a document, a section, a sentence or a footnote (sourceRules.firstHand), so citing one is WIKI_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED.
view.agents: Never returned by wiki_search or wiki_get: both read entries alone, and a document's ids are no entry's.
view.readers: The owner, on the user door. Another owner's space or document is a plain 404.

who.write: A maintenance run of the space (isWikiMaintenanceSession, maintenance.session) through the runner door, the server's docs_build job for an account it runs (build.server; origin maintenance, no session and no user), and an import the API server's container runs itself (origin import, no session and no user). For an account the server runs, a maintenance session is refused WIKI_SERVER_EXECUTES (build.server.door). Every other caller is refused WIKI_NOT_MAINTENANCE_SESSION, a headless call 400, another owner's space a plain 404; the user door has no write route. Every write asks requireConfirmedPlan first (plan.guard): with no confirmed plan it is WIKI_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED.
who.read: The owner, on the user door.

reads.directory: { spaceId, plan: { version, confirmedAt } | null, docs: { total, written }, categories }: the confirmed plan's categories in its order (number from 1), each with its documents (number <category>.<n>, title, question, written, status, updatedAt, planVersion, and lead: its two lines on the home, null for one not written — lead) and each document's sections (number, title, kind, written, stale). A space with no confirmed plan has none.
reads.doc: One document of the confirmed plan: its number, title, question, audience, scope (scopeOut's documents with their number and title), category, length, status, and when, from which plan version and at which origin/main commit (repoSha) it was written; its sections in the plan's order, each with the commit it was generated at and its blocks, a block's sentences each with its status, its footnote numbers, its new tokens and, once withdrawn, why, when, and through which entry or for which repository file (entryId, path — one of the two); its footnotes, numbered by first appearance — the same original and quote cited twice is one number — each with its kind, verdict, who checked it, its quote, its location (path@sha#Lstart-end, or <kind>:<record id>#c<start>-<end>) and what the page links to (links): a repository original's path, sha, lines, section, symbol and excerpt; a record's id (recordId), character range, session (sessionId, with recordId the pair a turn's, an event's or a tool call's deep link needs) and its title, number, time and label, task and project and their titles, a note's path; and its via entry; and the via entries as they stand now, with the footnotes each carried. A document of the plan not written yet is written false with its sections unwritten; one the plan does not have is a 404. counts and unsourcedShare are its sentences' as they stand.
reads.index: Every document of the confirmed plan, and every section whose title no other document of the plan shares — the ones every document has (known pitfalls, conventions, overview) are left out — each with its document's number and title, its category and whether it is written, in title order.
reads.writerState: { spaceId, planVersion, docs: [{ slug, planVersion, status, repoSha, updatedAt, sections: [{ key, materialSha256, repoSha, stale, generatedAt }] }] }: what is written, for a run to tell which sections to write again — a stale one, one whose material changed, or one whose repoSha origin/main has moved past in what it cites.
reads.writerDoc: One document as it is written, for a maintenance run of the space: the same answer as reads.doc, on the runner door. A run reads it to write a document's overview when the sections it summarizes were left unchanged, their sentences and footnotes as they stand.
reads.material: ?section=<key>, a section of the document in the confirmed plan: { spaceId, slug, section, planVersion, condition, entries, records, unresolved } — the server's half of the section's material (material): the section's session condition as the plan states it (null when it has none, and then nothing else), the entries it picked as the way in, and every record found through them or by the condition's projects, window and keywords, each redacted and placed. A section the confirmed plan's document does not have is a 404.
reads.affected: { spaceId, plan: { version, confirmedAt, repoSha, draftedAt } | null, build: { jobId, state, version } | null, sections: [{ doc, key, repoSha, generatedAt, stale, entryIds }], unplaced: [{ id, kind, title, summary, topics, anchorPaths, changedAt }], unplacedMore, proposed: { entryIds, commits, paths } } (WikiDocsAffected, affected): the confirmed plan (null with none: the run writes no document), the space's build that has not ended, the written sections to write again with the entries that fit them, the entries no section fits, and what the space's proposals already name — their entries, commits and the design documents their changes cite. repoSha is the commit the plan's references were last checked at: the confirmed version's, or the newest of the versions it was made from. A maintenance run's alone.

lead.means: A written document's lead on the directory (reads.directory): the first rules.sentences sentences of its first section — first as the confirmed plan orders its sections — in their order, withdrawn ones left out, joined as they read (a space after a Latin stop, none after a full-width one) and, past rules.maxChars characters, cut there with an ellipsis (…). The sentences' text as the document page has it, inline marks and all. Null for a document not written, and for one whose first section is not written or has no sentence that is not withdrawn.

requests.write: { planVersion, repoSha, model?, sections: [{ key, materialSha256, markdown, footnotes: [{ kind, path, sha, lines, section?, symbol?, quote?, excerpt?, verified, viaEntryId? } | { kind, ref, chars?, quote?, viaEntryId? }], dispositions?: [{ material, kind, ref, action, into, reason }] }] }
requests.withdraw: { repoSha, paths: [{ path, change: deleted | renamed, to? }] }: the origin/main commit the paths are gone at (40 hex), and at most affected.rules.withdrawPathsMax paths. Answered { spaceId, withdrawn, sections: [{ doc, key }] }: the sentences withdrawn now, and the sections they are in. Malformed is WIKI_DOC_INVALID with every error.

material.means: The server's half of a section's material (reads.material): what only the database has. The repository's half — design-document sections, code and contracts at origin/main — is read by the runner in its checkout (build.repository).
material.entries: The space's live entries (status active, anchor state neither changed nor missing) that fit the section's session condition (affected.fit), best first: an entry scores 3 for each keyword in its title, summary, fields or aliases, 2 when one of its anchors' paths is under one of anchorPaths, 1 when one of its topics is one of topics, 1 when its kind is one of entryKinds, and 1 when it was taken from one of projects; only one that fits is taken — a keyword or a path found it, or, of the condition's kinds, a topic or a project did — the newest first among equal scores, at most rules.entriesPerSection. Each is the way in to the records its current revision cites (at most rules.sourcesPerEntry of its live sources, in the order it cites them): an entry is never the material itself.
material.search: With projects and keywords both named, the owner's own words in them (a message or a steer isOwnerTurn reads as the owner's, in a project's coordinator session or a session of one of its tasks) and the comments on their tasks, within since..until (days, until included) and carrying one of the keywords, case aside: the ones carrying the most keywords first, the newest among equal, at most rules.ownerTurnsPerSection turns and rules.commentsPerSection comments.
material.projects: A condition's projects are ids, however the plan reached its reader. A stored version names each project by the id its reference resolved to (plan.gate.references); a read of a version (plan.reads.version) names each { id, title }. Every reader of a condition takes either as the id and leaves out anything that is no id: reads.material, the server's documents build (build.server.material), the maintenance run's documents step, which reads the plan through that read (maintenance.job.server), affected.fit, and the plan's own reads and gate. The runner path reads the plan's read and puts the projects' ids, alone and sorted, into a section's fingerprint (fingerprint), and takes the material from reads.material, which reads the stored condition: on both paths a section names the same projects and is handed the same material. (2026-10-09: the maintenance run's documents step passed the read's { id, title } on as ids, PostgreSQL refused them with 22P02, and the step wrote no section.)
material.records: Every record is read through the one reader a record has (WikiService.sourceText) and redacted with the shared redactor and the owner's workspace.env values, as a footnote's check reads it (verification.records). It is returned whole when it is at most rules.excerptChars long, and otherwise the rules.excerptChars around what found it — its entry source's quote, or the first keyword — with chars { start, end }: where the text is in the record's redacted text, in code points (a record footnote's chars). A record met twice is returned once, the first time. A source whose record is not one of this account's any more is listed under unresolved, never read.

weights.decision: the owner's own words: a message or steer isOwnerTurn reads as the owner's, an AskUserQuestion the owner answered, an owner's decision or comment
weights.merge: a record of what was merged or delivered: a merge receipt, an agent's delivery comment
weights.output: what a command or tool printed: a tool call (its command and output together), a tool's result, a background task's report
weights.error: what failed: a tool's error, an error event
weights.other: everything else: an agent's reply or thinking, another turn, a task, a note

material.weightsNote: The evidence weight the merge reads each record with: decision > merge > output > error, the newest first within one weight (owner 2026-09-28). A mechanism is the code's to settle, not a record's.

build.tool: none: a maintenance run's verb, CLI only, with no MCP tool beside it.
build.precondition: Build documents only as a Wiki maintenance run of the space, and only from the plan its owner confirmed: every footnote carries its verbatim quote, a repository quote is checked in the checkout at the commit it names, and a section whose material did not change is left as it is.
build.does: For each document of the confirmed plan (--doc, one of them; --section, one section of it), section by section: gathers the section's material — its design-document sections, code symbols and contracts from the checkout's origin/main (fetched first), and the server's half (reads.material) — takes out the platform's template messages and repeated texts, and keeps what fits rules.materialMaxChars, a mechanism's sections taking documents and code first and the others records first; fingerprints it (fingerprint) and leaves a section whose fingerprint is the one reads.writerState holds, and from which nothing was withdrawn, unwritten, without asking the model. Otherwise the local model merges the material (adopt, merge into another, drop, each with a reason; decision > merge > output > error, the newest first; the code settles a mechanism) and writes the section from the pieces it kept, a verbatim quote for every footnote it marks; a repository quote is looked for at the commit origin/main names, and its lines are the lines it was found at. Each section is written as soon as it is done, with its dispositions. A document's overview is written last, from its other sections as they are written, citing their footnotes and quotes and nothing else. It stops at the first 401 from the model's endpoint, and exits non-zero when any section it took up was left unwritten.
build.repository: A design document's section is its heading's lines up to the next heading of the same or a higher level; a code symbol its definition with the comment above it, up to where its braces close; a code path with no symbols named its head comment and the declarations whose words match the section; a directory the first files under it; a contract the file — each cut at a line boundary to fit, and read with git show at the commit origin/main names after the fetch (repoSha).
build.templates: A turn that begins About “ and says Orbit has not recorded it done is the project settlement card's message (the web composes it; the owner only presses the button), not the owner's words: it is filtered.
build.rulesNote: materialMaxChars is the most characters of material one section hands the model, each piece counted with materialHeaderChars for its header; the first piece is handed over whatever its size. parallel is the most sections of one document in flight at once.

server.who: An account the executor switch gives the server (jobs.executor: server, or canary with the account on its list). Under the default runner none of this runs: the owner's confirmation makes the build's task (plan.jobs.task), and orbit wiki docs build writes as this section says, word for word as before.
server.made: The owner's confirmation of a version asks for its build (plan.jobs.request). For such an account the build is made as a docs_build job of the wiki-worker (jobs.kindRuns.docs_build) instead of a task of the hidden list: the plan job made with the job's id (wiki_plan_job.job_id, no task_id) and the job queued at `priority` with input { planJobId }, in one transaction. A space whose maintenance names no workspace holds it, as on the runner path (plan.jobs.held.no_maintenance_workspace): the job reads the repository through that workspace's runner. The provider is not asked about, and the build does not wait behind the hidden list's unfinished task: no session's model is in it. A build made this way and still queued when the switch no longer gives the account to the server is cancelled, its plan job ended failed, by the space's next request for a build.
server.repository: The commit is origin/main as a snapshot names it (repoOps.kinds.snapshot, skipped when the space holds that commit's): the runner's fetch, as the command's own fetch was. The files a section's sources name are read whole at that commit (repoOps.kinds.read, no section: the whole file, cached by (space, sha, path) and read from the runner only once, packed into operations by the snapshot's sizes up to repoOps.read.operationBytes, `readsInFlight` operations at once, a failed one asked again up to `readAttempts` times in all), and the writer cuts a design document's section, a symbol, the declarations and a contract out of them exactly as `repository` says, at the same lines. A directory shows as git shows a tree, from the snapshot's paths, as the runner's git show did. A file larger than repoOps.read.wholeFileBytes is not read at all: it is missing with that reason, and a heading, symbol or contract in it says so. A space whose runner has not declared the whole-file capability reads each file only to repoOps.read.boundedChars (repoOps.looks runner_upgrade): a heading or a symbol past that window is missing and says so, and in such a file only the heading a section names, by its words or its number, is looked for, never one that merely contains the name, which could be another section. Each operation is waited for holding the job's lease (the exception repoOps.waiting names), at most `repoWaitSeconds`; a space whose runner cannot be asked (repoOps.looks no_workspace, runner_missing or runner_offline), and an operation past its limit, are infra failures, tried again.
server.shown: A file is shown only once its read has landed, as the runner's writer, which reads a file with git show when it shows it, never shows one unread. The sections of a document are built rules.parallel at a time and often name one file: a section whose file another section is already reading waits for that read, rather than starting none of its own and showing the file before it lands. (2026-10-09: version 27 named docs/article-durable-agent-work.md in several sections of one document, and every attempt of its build failed with «was shown before it was read».)
server.material: A section's session condition is read in process through src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-docs-material.ts, exactly as reads.material reads it: the entries it picks, the records they cite and the ones its projects, window and keywords find, each redacted with the owner's workspace.env values and placed.
server.calls: Every model call is a request through the queue (modelQueue): the system prompt `systemPrompt` (the runner's word for word), one user message, max_tokens `maxTokens`, the step one of `steps` — merge, write, rewrite (a paragraph marked only at its end, asked for once more), quotes (a footnote with no quote that holds, asked about once more) and overview — and a unit made of the document, the section and the sha256 of the prompt, so a replay reuses every answer whose question did not change. The queue retries a 5xx, a 429 and a dropped connection; a 401 stops the whole queue (modelQueue.retry). The prompts and every deterministic step — the filter, the cap, the fingerprint, the merge and the draft as read, the footnotes and their lines — are the runner's: src/shared/src/wiki-docs-build.fixture.json holds both implementations to one answer, written by src/runner-go/wiki_docs_build_fixture_test.go and read by src/apiserver/src/wiki-worker/wiki-docs-build-golden.spec.ts.
server.write: Through WikiDocs.write, the write route's own writer, as the server's own principal (origin maintenance, no session, no user: who.write): one section a write, the run's writes one at a time, model the System model's name. A refusal (WIKI_DOC_INVALID, WIKI_PLAN_STALE, WIKI_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED) fails its section, in the runner's words.
server.progress: As each document is taken up and at the end: the plan job's progress (plan.jobs.progress, a build's { docs: { done, total }, current }) and the job's own (jobs.progress: { step: snapshot | documents, docs, current }).
server.end: Every section it took up written or unchanged: the plan job ends succeeded with the confirmed version it wrote and the build's report (plan.jobs.buildReport), and the job succeeds with the run's summary as its report. A section left unwritten: the other sections are tried, then the plan job ends failed (`<n> sections were left unwritten`) and the job fails as content, its report on the row — as the command exited non-zero. A failure of the platform (the runner away, an operation or a request past its limit, the worker stopping) ends neither: the job is tried again and replays, and a section already written is left as it is by its fingerprint. A replay that finds its plan job already ended answers with that end.
server.door: For such an account the documents' runner-door routes (routes.writerState, writerDoc, material, write, affected and withdraw) refuse a maintenance session WIKI_SERVER_EXECUTES before anything is read — as the plan job's routes refuse every session, a build job's included (plan.jobs.server.door) — so an older runner's orbit wiki docs build, and a maintenance run's documents step, ask their session's model nothing. Any other session is WIKI_NOT_MAINTENANCE_SESSION as before. Under runner they answer exactly as routes says.
server.runnerCli: orbit wiki docs build reads WIKI_SERVER_EXECUTES as the server building the documents — at its first call, the job read, as at any of the documents' routes: it asks no model, writes nothing more, says so (`serverExecutes` in --json) and exits 0. A build task's run, made before the switch, is refused at that first call and its job ends with its task; an end refused because the switch moved mid-run is left to the task too. It ships with the next runner release; until then a runner exits non-zero on the refusal, having asked nothing.
server.systemPrompt: 你是 Orbit 的技术文档作者。你只根据给你的材料写，不编造事实、名字、数字和路径。用中文写，代码名、路径、命令保留原文。只输出要求的内容。

docs.tool: none: no MCP tool reads or writes a document. Writing is a maintenance run's verb on the CLI; reading is the owner's, in the Wiki.

systemModel.why: The wiki's model calls move off the runner (design section 0): the server's wiki-worker calls the deployment's own System model, whose address and key are in that service's environment and nowhere else. At this phase the worker only probes the model and writes its state and heartbeat; P1b adds the job table (jobs), the request queue (modelQueue) and the executor switch (jobs.executor); the pipelines call the model their own way until the phases that move them (P3-P8) send their calls through the queue.

service.name: wiki-worker
service.context: NestFactory.createApplicationContext over WikiWorkerModule: Prisma and the worker's own providers, no controller and no port; enableShutdownHooks().
service.dependsOn: apiserver, service_healthy: the worker runs no migration, the apiserver applies them on boot.

envRules.configured: baseUrl, apiKey and model all set: an http or https URL, a key, a model name. With any of them missing or unusable the state is unconfigured and nothing is probed or called.
envRules.concurrency: Model requests in flight at once across every space, held by the request queue (modelQueue.concurrency). A value that is not a positive whole number is read as the default.
envRules.onlyOn: wiki-worker. The apiserver's environment holds none of the four (docker-compose.yml, test/compose-topology.test.mjs).
envRules.names: None is ANTHROPIC_*: Compose prefers the shell's environment to .env, and an agent session's environment carries those names (src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-compose-env.spec.ts).
envRules.problems: readWikiSystemModel(env) returns the configuration and the problems it found, and the worker logs them once. Neither the problems nor the log carry the key.

request.body: {model, max_tokens, system, messages: [one user message], stream: true}. Every call gives its max_tokens explicitly; no tools are sent and thinking is not turned on.
request.eventRules: The answer is the text of the text_delta deltas, in order. message_start carries the model and the first usage, message_delta the stop reason and the usage so far. A call has ended only at message_stop: a stream that closes before it is a dropped connection. ping, content_block_start, content_block_stop and any event not named here are read past.
request.usage: inputTokens and outputTokens are the last values the stream reported: message_delta's, else message_start's.
request.timeouts: Each call has a budget of its own, its step's limit (verify, extract, import and articles 15 minutes, docs 20, plan 60), and is disconnected after idleTimeoutSeconds without a byte whatever its budget. Both, and a cancel, abort it through one AbortController.
request.partial: The text received so far is handed to the caller after every delta, and carried by the error of a call that fails: what the request queue keeps as a request's partial (P1b).

errors.retryable: HTTP 5xx and 429; a connection refused, reset or closed, a name that does not resolve, a stream closed before message_stop, idleTimeoutSeconds without a byte; an SSE error event of type overloaded_error, api_error or rate_limit_error.
errors.unauthorized: HTTP 401, or an SSE error event of type authentication_error: the key was refused, and the state becomes auth_failed.
errors.other: Every other HTTP status and SSE error, an answer that is not an event stream, the call's own budget running out, and a cancel.

request.connections: Node's own fetch: connections are kept alive and reused, with no per-origin limit below the concurrency. After message_stop the stream is still read to its end, for a second at most, so that the connection goes back to the pool.

health.headers: authorization and anthropic-version, as a call sends them.
health.rule: An answer in upStatuses is up and one in authFailedStatuses auth_failed; any other status, no answer within timeoutSeconds, or no connection is down. Probed every intervalSeconds while configured, and each probe writes the state and the heartbeat together.

status.row: Exactly one, id 1, written by the worker alone with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE. The apiserver only reads it.

meaning.up: The probe answered one of health.upStatuses.
meaning.down: The probe got no answer, or another status. Requests are not taken while down (modelQueue.pause); the probe goes on, and the next up resumes them.
meaning.auth_failed: The endpoint refused the key (401), to the probe or to a call. It holds until the worker restarts, which is when a corrected key is read: every later call would be refused the same way.
meaning.unconfigured: env.baseUrl, env.apiKey or env.model is missing or unusable. Nothing is probed or called; the heartbeat is still written.

status.since: When the state began: kept while the state and the model stay what they were.
status.lastError: Why the state is not up, in words that name neither the address nor the key: an HTTP status, a connection error's code, a variable's name. Null while up.
status.checkedAt: When the probe last ran; null while unconfigured.
status.workerSeenAt: The worker's heartbeat, written with every probe, every health.intervalSeconds.

read.who: Any account the wiki is on for (JwtAuthGuard and WikiRolloutGuard; a personal access token needs wiki:read): it is the deployment's model, not a space's. It writes nothing.
read.workerNotRunning: No row, or a workerSeenAt older than status.workerStaleSeconds, reads as worker_not_running: what the settings page and the health line show as wiki worker not running. since is then the last heartbeat.
read.executor: The executor switch as it stands for the caller (jobs.executor.read, P9): { mode, serverExecutes } — what the wiki settings page reads to draw the System model instead of the provider. The other five fields are the deployment's and read the same for every account.
read.never: The System model's address, its key, and last_error: the read says the model's name and its state, and nothing else.

series.orbit_wiki_model_state: gauge, label state (one of read.states): 1 for the state the read answers, 0 for the others.
series.orbit_wiki_worker_heartbeat_age_seconds: gauge: seconds since workerSeenAt; absent while no worker has written.
series.orbit_wiki_model_calls_total: counter, label outcome (succeeded, or one of request.errors): the queue's calls, read from its rows at scrape time (modelQueue.metrics).
series.orbit_wiki_model_call_duration_seconds: summary, quantiles 0.5 and 0.95: how long the queue's calls ran, over the rows that ended (modelQueue.metrics).

jobs.why: The wiki's pipelines move off the runner's maintenance sessions onto the server (design section 0). A unit of that work is a job: the server makes one, a wiki-worker claims it, and the model calls it makes go through the persisted request queue (modelQueue). At this phase the table, the claim, the lease, the retry and the executor switch are the contract; the seven pipeline kinds arrive with the phases that implement them (P3 to P8), and the one kind that runs today is `smoke`.

kindRuns.articles: The server's articles writer (P4, articles.serverExecution): orbit wiki articles done by the wiki worker with the System model. Its input is {}; it is made after a maintenance run of the space by the rule articles.regeneration states, at priority 0 (articles.job). It reads the plan, takes up the topics whose fingerprint changed, groups a big topic as the runner does, has the model name the groups and write the articles through the queue — step articles, a unit per topic, fingerprint and part — and writes them through WikiArticles.write. Its ref is the space's snapshot's sha, asked for once and parked on when there is none (repoOps.waiting). It succeeds when every topic it took up is written or unchanged, and fails as content, its report on the row, when one was left unwritten.
kindRuns.smoke: One model call, its answer and usage written into the job's report: the shortest route through the queue, and P1's end-to-end proof that claim, call, write-back and settle work together. It runs no pipeline and reads nothing; its input is { system?, prompt?, maxTokens? }, each with a default. A kind whose phase has not landed stays queued — the claim takes only the kinds the worker's build runs — so no deployment is handed work it would have to fail.
kindRuns.import: orbit wiki import's reading, on the server (P5, import.server): the notes the command registered, read by the System model through the queue — one request a note (step import, unit the note), one retry with what did not hold up (step import_retry) — checked as the runner checks them, the anchors held to the space's snapshot, then a dry run and one proposal with origin import as the calling session, under a key made of the space and the ops. Its input is the create route's body with the session in it; its report is import.server.report, which the command prints and remembers. Made only by the runner door's create route, at import.server.priority.
kindRuns.verify: The server's verifier (P3, design section 8 and agentSurface.verify.serverExecution): the ops an Automatic space holds back, verified by the wiki worker with the System model in place of the session's own provider.
