Its input is { sessionId } — the session whose waiting ops it verifies, which is the identity a verdict has to be reported under — and it runs the runner's verifier step by step: read reviewModes.verification.list for that session (rules.verificationListMax at a time, the server's own evidence reader), build the one-op prompt with the entries numbered E1..En (agentSurface.verify.prompt), ask the System model through the queue — one request per op, step verify, unit the op's id, so a replayed job reuses the answers it holds — and report each verdict through WikiService.recordVerifications, the one writer, as soon as it is read. An answer that is not a verdict is reported as nothing and counted in the report ({ looked, verified, supported, partial, unsupported, duplicate, failed, failures[{opId, why, refused}], stopped, usage }); the job still succeeds, because the ops that got verdicts are its result, and those left without one keep waiting. A space that is no longer automatic ends the pass where it stands (verification.notAutomatic), and a call whose request ends in a way that is not the platform's (the queue's own classes) is that op's failure, not the pass's. The two passes a maintenance run makes and the adoption of ended sessions' ops (verification.adoption) are arguments of the same function, P8's to call.
kindRuns.plan_draft: A draft of the space's plan on the server (P6, plan.jobs.server): the four steps of plan.jobs.run — the catalogue, each category's details, each document's outline, the rules' draft — through the queue, gated on the space's snapshot and by the plan's gate, three rounds at most; stored as a version the wiki_job authored. Its input is { planJobId }; its report is { kind, planJobId, outcome, version, error, plan: plan.jobs.report }. Made by advanceWikiPlanJob for a draft the space's creation or its owner asked for, at plan.jobs.server.priority.
kindRuns.plan_revise: A revision of the space's plan on the server (P6, plan.jobs.server): plan.jobs.run.revise through the queue — the new catalogue with what each document is made from and the conventions it moves, then the documents that merge or are new — gated as plan_draft is. Its input and report are plan_draft's; the owner's instructions are the plan job's own. Made by advanceWikiPlanJob for the owner's redraft with instructions.
kindRuns.docs_build: The documents' build on the server (P7, docs.build.server): what orbit wiki docs build did in a build job's session, done by the wiki-worker with the System model. Made by the owner's confirmation of a plan version for an account the server runs, instead of the build's task (plan.jobs.server), at docs.build.server.priority; its input is { planJobId }. It reads the repository at a snapshot's commit through the space's runner, the records through the material read, writes each section through the docs write route's writer, says how far it got and how it ended on its plan job, and fails as content when a section was left unwritten.
kindRuns.maintain: A space's Wiki maintenance run on the server (P8, maintenance.job.server): what a task's session ran with `orbit wiki maintain` until P10, done by the wiki-worker with the deployment's System model and the space's snapshot. Its input is { runId } — the wiki_maintenance_run the trigger made beside it, which carries why the run was made, how far it must read and how the space stood — and the job executes exactly that run: the dossiers through WikiMaintenance.dossierPage, one request per dossier through the queue (step extract, unit the session's id, at most rules.extractConcurrency in flight), the checks and the one retry of wiki-maintain.ts, the dry run and then the batches of at most limits.opsPerChangeset ops with the run's own breaker (wiki-maintain-job.ts), the cursor advance through WikiMaintenance.advanceRecorded, its own ops verified twice and then up to rules.adoptOpsMax adopted (P3's verifyWikiOps with a maintenance-job principal), the anchors as one wiki_repo_op, and the documents' step (maintenance.job.docs) with P7's writer and P6's plan gate. It reports maintenance.job.report plus the token spend, and its end queues the articles a successful run owes (articles.regeneration). A failure of the platform is thrown as infra and the job is tried again without counting against the space; a failure of the work ends the run (outcome failed, the space's streak one higher) and the job fails as content (§5.5).

jobs.waitingRule: Nothing writes `waiting` yet: this phase's worker keeps a job running while its model request waits, and the request's wait limit is what ends it. The transitions that park a job — on a repo operation (P2), or on the model being away — arrive with the phases that need them, and a waiting row holds no lease (the CHECK above).

lease.claim: One statement per claim, the shape watch_delivery's claim has: UPDATE wiki_job … FROM (SELECT … WHERE state = 'queued' AND (next_attempt_at IS NULL OR next_attempt_at <= now()) AND attempts < retry.maxAttempts AND kind = ANY(the kinds this build runs) AND owner_id matches what this worker serves AND NOT EXISTS a running job of the same space … ORDER BY priority DESC, created_at, id LIMIT n FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) — each claimed row gets a new lease_generation, and started_at is the first claim's.
lease.hosts: lease_owner, lease_generation and lease_deadline_at are set together exactly while the row is running (`wiki_job_lease_chk` holds it both ways), and every settle clears them.
lease.cas: Every write that ends an attempt — succeeded, requeued, failed — is a compare-and-set on the claim's generation. A worker whose lease ran out and was taken over matches no row and settles nothing.
lease.sweep: A running job whose lease_deadline_at passed goes back to queued, attempts one higher and the next attempt on retry.backoffSeconds; the takeover starts the job from the beginning, and the request rows it already made answer the replay (modelQueue.identity).

jobs.onePerSpace: At most one job per space runs at a time (design section 5.1, the hidden list's maxConcurrent 1): the claim skips a space whose job is running, and a partial unique index over space_id WHERE state = 'running' is the same rule in the database, for two schedulers that read at once. A job that is waiting (waiting_for set) holds no lease and does not occupy the space.
jobs.priority: Integer, default 0. Owner-initiated work — a plan draft, a review, a build, an import from the command line — is made with a higher priority than background maintenance, and the claim takes the highest first; within one priority, the longest-waiting job first. A verify job is made with 1: the session that proposed the op is waiting for it, and the space knows nothing of what was proposed until the verdict arrives; the pass a maintenance run makes over what ended sessions left waiting (verification.adoption, P8) is background work at 0.

retry.rule: An infra failure puts the job back to queued with attempts one higher and next_attempt_at now plus backoffSeconds[attempts], the same schedule the queue's calls use. A content failure ends it: state failed, failure_kind content, ended_at set. attempts counts the infra retries of the job's own row.
retry.limit: No job is put back for ever (2026-10-09: a docs_build job whose writer failed an assertion was put back every time its space was free). When the attempt that makes maxAttempts fails as infra, the job is ended instead of requeued: state failed, failure_kind infra, ended_at set, attempts counting that attempt, and on its row the error `Ended after <n> attempts: <the last attempt's error>` (2,000 characters at most), which Activity's Runs card shows (read). An error the build did not expect, which is neither the platform's nor the work's (a failed assertion, a TypeError), is retried as infra in case it was passing, but ends the job the same way at the attempt that makes unexpectedMaxAttempts, its error saying it was unexpected. The executor ends the attempt it settles. An attempt the lease sweep or a repository wait counted at the limit is never claimed (lease.claim), and the worker's next pass ends the job. A job ended this way settles what waits on it in the same transaction, as the rollback sweep does (executor.rollback; settleWikiJobRows in wiki-worker/wiki-jobs.ts): its calls and repository operations still queued or running are cancelled, a maintain job's run ends failed / infra with the error (the space's streak is not touched, and the next run reads again what this one did not take in), and the plan job of a plan_draft, plan_revise or docs_build job ends failed with the error, still naming its wiki_job: the plan page reads the draft or build as failed, and the owner's next request makes a new one.

jobs.startup: A worker runs one pass the moment it starts — sweep, then claim — so a job left queued or handed back by a dead worker is picked up where it stands.
jobs.make: The pipelines enqueue a job as a row (kind, input, priority, state queued) when the executor switch says the server runs for that account. The phases that move each pipeline add their own route or trigger: since P3 a submission that recorded an op an Automatic space holds back (reviewModes.verification.waits) makes a verify job for the session that proposed it, after its own transaction commits, at the waiting priority (priority above) — and so does the owner reopening ops a verdict should not have decided (verification.reopen), whose sessions are usually long gone — with one queued job per session and space, since a job reads the ops that wait when it runs (a later submission rides it, while an op arriving mid-run gets a job of its own); since P5 the runner door's import-jobs route makes an `import` job (import.server.create); since P4 an articles job is also made, where the server records the end of a maintenance run of an account it runs, by the rule articles.regeneration states (articles.serverExecution.made); since P6 a plan job of the account is made as a `plan_draft` or `plan_revise` job (plan.jobs.server.make); since P7 the owner's confirmation of a plan version makes a docs_build job for an account the server runs, in place of the build's task (docs.build.server.made); and smoke is made by the specs directly.
jobs.progress: A job's progress column is its own pipeline's to write (a step, a count, what it is doing), under its lease generation; report is what it ends with. The smoke job writes a report; the import job writes both (import.server.progress, import.server.report); the articles job writes its report (articles.serverExecution.ends), and so does the verify job (jobs.kindRuns.verify); the plan jobs write both (plan.jobs.server.progress, plan.jobs.server.finish), and so does the docs_build job (docs.build.server.progress, docs.build.server.end).

rules.runner: The old path only: maintenance sessions and their tasks run the pipelines, and no worker claims or executes a wiki job. Nothing about today's behavior changes.
rules.canary: The accounts ORBIT_WIKI_EXECUTOR_CANARY_OWNERS lists (comma-separated uuids) are run by the server's worker; every other account is as under runner.
rules.server: Every account is. The switch gates execution only: rows written by either path stay where they are, and moving it back to runner stops new jobs being taken without deleting anything.

executor.mistyped: A value that is none of the three is read as runner, with a logged problem: a switch reached for and mistyped must land on the path that already runs, never on one whose worker nobody deployed.
executor.whoReadsIt: One pure function (src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-executor-switch.ts, shaped after wiki-rollout.ts) is read by the apiserver and by the wiki-worker, so both answer the same about an account. The variables reach a service the way the model's do — compose passes them from the deployment's .env to both the apiserver and the wiki-worker (P3 wired them; test/compose-topology.test.mjs pins the two lines, and src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-compose-env.spec.ts holds them to names no agent session carries), and unset everywhere reads as runner. Setting the switch is the account owner's: production stays runner until P10.

read.rule: What a read tells the account that asks (wikiExecutorView): mode is the deployment's switch, one of modes, and serverExecutes whether the server executes this account's wiki — mode server, or canary with the account on its list. Never the list itself, nor whether any other account is on it.
read.readBy: systemModel.read (executor) and maintenance.health (executor): the clients draw the server's settings, the Runs card and the status line's server reasons while serverExecutes holds, and under runner — or from a control plane that predates the field — exactly what they drew before.

rollback.phase: server execution, rollback — the 2026-10-08 production incident
rollback.when: Moving the switch back to runner, or removing an account from the canary list, recreates the apiserver and the wiki-worker (docs/configuration.md), and the apiserver's start runs one sweep (wiki/wiki-executor-sweep.ts) that cancels every wiki_job of an account the switch no longer serves that is still queued, running or waiting. The worker never claims such a row — its claim filters by the switch's owners — so nothing else would ever end it: on 2026-10-08 the maintain job left running held its space's maintenance on both paths until it was cancelled by hand. The sweep is the apiserver's, not the worker's — the apiserver is the process the stuck job blocked — and every write matches only the rows still in flight, so a sweep that runs twice, or that races a worker settling its last write, changes nothing a run already ended.
rollback.job: state cancelled, ended_at set, waiting_for and the lease columns cleared, the reason on its row: the switch no longer serves the account and the in-flight job was cancelled at apiserver start.
rollback.request: Every wiki_model_request of the job still queued or running: state cancelled, ended_at set, error, error_kind, partial, not_before and the lease columns cleared — the 0401 constraints make those a queued or running row's, so a cancelled row's are NULL, and a succeeded row is untouched.
rollback.repoOp: Every wiki_repo_op of the job still queued or running: state cancelled, ended_at set, the reason on its row, the claim (lease_owner, claimed_at, heartbeat_at, runner_id) cleared — no runner spends work on a result nobody will read.
rollback.maintain: The run row the job names (input.runId) is ended failed / infra with the reason, only while it has no outcome. The failure is the platform's, not the pipeline's: the space's streak (wiki_cursor.consecutive_failures, written only when a run advances the cursor) is not touched, and the cursor did not move, so the next run — the runner path's, after the rollback — re-reads what this one never took in.
rollback.plan: The plan job the job names (input.planJobId) is ended failed with the reason, still naming its wiki_job (a made or ended plan job must name its maker, 0405), so the owner's next request is made on the path that runs now. A docs_build job's plan job is settled the same way.
rollback.verify: Nothing else is written. An op left verifying waits by design: the next maintenance run of the space adopts it (reviewModes.verification.adoption.who), which after the rollback is the runner path's run.
rollback.articlesImportSmoke: Nothing else is written. Articles resume by the rule articles.regeneration states; an import's proposed ops wait for their verdicts the same way, and the polling command reads the job's end; a smoke job has no rows of its own.
rollback.trigger: Until the sweep has run — and as the rule after every rollback — the maintenance trigger asks unfinishedMaintainJob only of an account the server executes: a server job of an unserved account must not hold the space's runner-path task. On 2026-10-08 one did, and the space had no maintenance at all until the job was cancelled by hand.

runRows.why: Health and the day's count read runs, not the history of how they were made (design section 5.1).
runRows.doctor: wiki_maintenance_run.job_id and wiki_plan_job.job_id record the job that ran a run; task_id is nullable from 0401 on, and a CHECK requires exactly one maker per started row (a plan job is exempt while it is queued or held — it has made neither yet).
runRows.count: The day's runs (space.settings.maintenance.dailyRunLimit) count the maintenance list's tasks made since midnight UTC, as they always have, and the runs made by a job read off their own rows, which have no task; a run in active catch-up on a local endpoint and one that failed are not counted, whichever path made it. Plan jobs never count.

jobs.runnerTurns: A server run creates no task and no session: it does not touch runnerActiveTurns, and the runner's only part in the server path is the repo operations of P2.

read.who: The space's owner on the user door (JwtAuthGuard and WikiRolloutGuard; a personal access token needs wiki:read): another account's space is the plain 404. It writes nothing.
read.why: A server run has no task and no session to open (design section 2.2): what it is doing — its step, its calls, where they wait — is on Activity, and this read is what the Runs card and a run's page draw.
read.answer: { spaceId, jobs }: the space's newest limits.jobs rows of wiki_job, newest first by created_at.

jobRules.ahead: While the job is queued: how many queued jobs of the deployment the claim takes before it (priority DESC, created_at, id — lease.claim's order); null in every other state.
jobRules.progress: The pipeline's own progress (jobs.progress) as { step, done, total }: done and total as the pipeline wrote them, or for the import's shape (import.server.progress) the notes read or failed against the notes it was handed; null when the pipeline wrote none.
jobRules.calls: Its calls counted by state — total, queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled — and the input and output tokens they reported, over every one of its rows.
jobRules.nextCall: Of its queued calls, the one the queue reaches first: { ahead, enqueuedAt }, ahead counted as request.ahead is; null while none waits.
jobRules.requests: Its newest limits.callsPerJob calls by enqueued_at, given oldest first; calls.total counts the ones left out.

requestRules.ahead: While the call is queued: how many queued requests of the deployment the queue takes before it (priority DESC, enqueued_at, id — modelQueue.concurrency.claim's order), whoever they are for; null in every other state.
requestRules.times: How long a call waited is from enqueuedAt to startedAt (or to now while it is queued), and how long it ran from startedAt to endedAt (or to now while it runs); startedAt is its first claim's, so a retry's time is the call's own.

read.never: A call's request (system prompt, prompt, max_tokens), its request_sha256, answer and partial; the lease columns of either table; the job's input and report; whose the runs and calls ahead in a queue are; and the System model's address or key, which no row of either table holds (systemModel.request.errors: the queue's words name neither).

modelQueue.why: All of the wiki's model calls go through one persisted queue, so that a deployment's System model answers at most ORBIT_WIKI_MODEL_CONCURRENCY requests at once whatever the pipelines were doing when a worker died (design section 0). The row is also the breakpoint: a pipeline replayed after a restart reuses the answer a finished call holds instead of issuing it again.
modelQueue.identity: (job_id, step, unit, attempt) is unique, and the pair (step, unit) is the call's own address inside its job: enqueuing it again MEETS the row it already has rather than making a second call. `attempt` is which attempt of that unit the row is (a genuine redo moves to the next), and `attempts` is how many times this row has been tried — a lease that ran out and a retry each count one, and the backoff reads it.
modelQueue.request: { system, prompt, maxTokens } — the call exactly as the client sends it, and its sha256, so the same unit twice with a different call can be told from the same call replayed.

concurrency.meaning: Requests in flight at once across every space and every worker of the deployment.
concurrency.claim: One transaction per scheduler: pg_advisory_xact_lock (one key for the whole queue), count the rows whose state is running and whose lease has not expired, then claim at most (concurrency − that count) — ORDER BY priority DESC, enqueued_at, id LIMIT that many FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, each row under a new lease generation. However many workers run, running-plus-unexpired never passes the concurrency, and two schedulers claiming at once serialize on the lock rather than on rows.

modelQueue.priority: Integer, default 0, copied from the job. Owner-initiated work sorts above background maintenance, and within one priority the longest-waiting request goes first; perJob caps what one job can hold in flight, so no single job takes the queue.

lease.rule: A running row holds lease_owner, lease_generation and lease_deadline_at together (`wiki_model_request_lease_chk`), renewed while the call runs. The text received so far is written back with a renewal only when it grew, so a row that dies mid-call keeps what had arrived.
lease.sweep: A running row whose lease passed goes back to queued with attempts one higher and its partial KEPT; the next claim re-issues the call and hands the client the text it had. Every settle is a compare-and-set on the claim's generation, so a takeover's generation is not the dead worker's and its late write settles nothing.
lease.answer: A succeeded row's answer is written once, by the claim that owned it: an answer that arrives after the lease was taken over is dropped, and the takeover issues the call again.

retry.rule: 5xx, 429 and connection failures class retryable: the row goes back to queued, attempts one higher, not_before now plus backoffSeconds[attempts − 1] (0, then 10 s, then 30 s and every one after it). Nothing else is retried: the call's own budget running out, an answer that is not an event stream and an unclassified error end the request (state failed, error_kind other) and the job reads it.
retry.unauthorized: A 401 (and an authentication_error event) is its own case: the request goes back to the queue — it is the deployment's key to fix, not the work's to lose — and the worker reports the refusal to the model's state, which turns auth_failed and stops the queue (pause).

waitLimit.rule: How long a request may wait from its enqueue before it fails, by its step (the step's own name or one of its stages: extract*, docs*, import*, plan*). A request that waits past it ends failed with error_kind other and the wait limit's words; the job that made it reads that and fails as infra, so a model that is away for an hour ends a run rather than hanging it forever. The clock is the row's enqueued_at: a retry does not start it over.

callBudget.rule: One call's own budget, by step (design section 6): the call is disconnected when it runs out, and is also disconnected after the contract's idleTimeoutSeconds without a byte (systemModel.request).

pause.when: The model's state is not up (wiki_model_status): down and auth_failed both stop the claim, so requests stay queued and undelivered (design section 5.3).
pause.resume: down resumes by itself — the probe keeps asking, and the next up makes the next pass claim again. auth_failed holds until the worker restarts with a corrected key, which is when every later call would stop being refused.

shutdown.plan: A, the owner's decision of 2026-10-07: the worker does not wait for calls in flight.
shutdown.rule: Stop claiming; abort each call in flight; each saves the text it had into partial and sets its lease_deadline_at to now, so the next process's sweep takes the row over at once and re-issues the call with what had arrived. A job interrupted the same way lets its lease out to now, and its kind's pipeline is what decides, from the request rows, whether an interrupted call is continued or redone.

notify.rule: A settled request sends pg_notify on the channel with its id, and the worker that made it LISTENs on one dedicated connection (the shape realtime.service.ts uses) so the waiting job wakes as the answer lands.
notify.fallback: pollSeconds: a waiter re-reads its row on that interval whatever the announcements did, so a notification that never arrived costs latency and never an answer.

series.orbit_wiki_model_calls_total: counter, label outcome (succeeded, or one of systemModel.request.errors): read from the queue's rows at scrape time — a succeeded row is `succeeded`, a failed row its error's class, and a request that failed and was requeued counts under that failure's class until it succeeds or the wait limit ends it.
series.orbit_wiki_model_call_duration_seconds: summary, quantiles 0.5 and 0.95: how long the queue's calls ran (started_at to ended_at), over the rows that ended.
series.orbit_wiki_model_queue_depth: gauge: requests queued, waiting for a slot.
series.orbit_wiki_model_requests_in_flight: gauge: requests running right now, their lease unexpired — never above concurrency.claims.
series.orbit_wiki_model_request_wait_seconds: summary, quantiles 0.5 and 0.95: how long settled calls waited from their enqueue to their first byte.
series.orbit_wiki_model_request_run_seconds: summary, quantiles 0.5 and 0.95: how long settled calls ran.
series.orbit_wiki_model_request_tokens_total: counter, label direction (input, output): tokens the succeeded calls spent.
series.orbit_wiki_model_request_errors_total: counter, label status: failed calls by the HTTP status that refused them, `none` for a failure with no answer (a connection, a timeout).

repoOps.why: The server runs the wiki's pipelines but never touches a repository: the credentials are on the runners (design section 1.4). A step that needs to know what the repository says asks the machine its space's workspace runs on, and the answer comes back through a row — no session, no concurrency slot and no model call on the runner (G2).

kindRuns.snapshot: Everything the server asks of one commit at once: fetch origin/main, resolve the sha, and build the index the pipelines query — every path with its size, every document's title and headings, every source file's symbols, the commits reachable from origin/main, and the README's first paragraph. A sha the server already holds is not sent again (`input.skipSha`). Above `fragments.inlineBytes` it travels in fragments.
kindRuns.read: The whole text of named paths at a named sha — the file itself, not a window of it (owner 2026-10-08). One file may be up to `read.wholeFileBytes` (2 MB); a larger one is not read at all: its item answers found: false with reason `too_large` and its size, and the pipelines treat it as missing and say why. An answer larger than `fragments.inlineBytes` travels in fragments as a snapshot's index does, and is reassembled by its sha256 and byte count before anything is cached. What a pipeline gives the model is cut server-side by `read.docSectionChars`, `read.contractChars` and `read.sectionChars`; those are cutting rules, not read limits. A runner that has not declared `readCapability` answers with the old window: at most `read.boundedChars` characters an item, the whole request answering `read.sectionChars`, its end marked `truncated`.
kindRuns.diff: `git diff --name-status -M` between two commits, and the design documents the range added or copied (`--diff-filter=AR -- docs/`) — what a maintenance run looks for.
kindRuns.anchors: The anchor checks a maintenance run already makes (`src/runner-go/wiki_anchors.go`), reused: a path exists, a symbol's region hashes as it is held to, a commit is reachable from the snapshot's commit set.

dispatch.claim: One statement per heartbeat: UPDATE wiki_repo_op … FROM (SELECT … JOIN workspace w ON w.id = o.workspace_id WHERE w.runner_id = this runner AND (state = 'queued' OR (state = 'running' AND heartbeat_at < now - staleSeconds AND lease_owner IS DISTINCT FROM this process)) ORDER BY created_at, id LIMIT n FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) — every claimed row a new claim_generation.
dispatch.route: workspace.runner_id: an operation is handed only to the machine the space's workspace runs on, and the workspace's work_dir travels with it.
dispatch.wake: The enqueue NOTIFYs the runner wake channel, so the machine beats at once instead of on its 30-second tick.

routes.result: POST /runner/wiki/repo-ops/:id/result — fenced on (lease_owner, claim_generation) and the runner token; a write from a claim that was taken over answers 409 STALE_CLAIM and settles nothing.
routes.progress: POST /runner/wiki/repo-ops/:id/progress — the heartbeat renewal that keeps a long operation from being taken over.
routes.fragments: POST /runner/wiki/repo-ops/:id/fragments — one call per fragment, fenced the same way, staged on the operation until its result arrives.

fragments.why: The API's request body is capped at 10 MB (src/apiserver/src/main.ts) and a plan's repository index is larger than that (design section 4.3). A snapshot that fits travels inside the result; one that does not is uploaded in fragments and reassembled — by sha256, and by the byte count the result names — before it becomes the space's snapshot. A read's answer is the same: above inlineBytes the whole answer (whole files and all) is staged as fragments of the operation and reassembled there.

cache.perSpace: One snapshot per space, replaced whole when a newer one lands: the index and the fragments it is kept in. Owner-scoped like everything else, and deleted with the space (the composite foreign key into wiki_space). The files read at a sha are kept one row per (space, sha, path) and are the same: a file already held is never read from the runner again, a snapshot landing drops every row of another sha, and the space's deletion takes them with it.
cache.visibility: The owner's and nobody else's: no route returns it, and what reaches the System model reaches it through the same redactor the notes go through (design section 9).

repoOps.safety: An operation checks its checkout before it reads it: the repository's origin URL must be the space's `repo.urlNorm` and the checkout's root commit must be the space's `rootCommitSha`. Otherwise it fails, says which repository it found, and reads nothing.
repoOps.waiting: A job that needs a repository operation is parked (wiki_job state waiting, waiting_for 'repo', no lease) and woken by a NOTIFY on the wiki_repo_op channel when the operation settles. A runner that has not declared `wiki-repo-op/v1` is handed nothing: the operation stays queued, the job stays parked until its wait limit, and the space's health line says the runner has to be upgraded. The import's snapshot (import.server.snapshot) is the exception: it is waited for holding the job's lease, a bounded wait with a fallback, so a runner that is away costs the import its fresh anchors and never the run. The documents' build (docs.build.server.repository) waits for its snapshot and its reads the same way, each bounded by docs.build.server.repoWaitSeconds: they are many and short, and a job parked on each would replay the build each time; one past its limit fails the attempt as infra.

refusals.when: The wiki is off for this account (ORBIT_WIKI rollout).
The calling session's workspace is bound to no space and could not be bound on first use. The message says in one sentence how the owner binds it.

The op, its entry, its anchors or its sources do not have the shape this contract gives them: a kind's fields (KIND_SPECS), a limit, a phase-3 kind, an amend of a decision, a baseRevision where one is required or forbidden, a source ref of a kind in sourceInput.rowIdKinds that is neither spelling of an id. errors[] names every field that failed.
A non-owner op adds, amends or supersedes a kind only the owner writes (kinds.<kind>.ownerOnlyOps).
A source does not resolve among the owner's own rows (errors[] names it by its path), cites a wiki entry or view, or an op that must cite a source cites none.
A quote, whitespace-normalized, is not a substring of the text of the record it cites.
An amend, supersede or retire names a baseRevision that is not the entry's current revision. The answer carries the current revision and a diff.

The op is past limits.opsPerChangeset in its request; or it would wait for the owner and pass limits.opsPerTurn for the request or limits.opsPerSession for the calling session (limitNotes.quota); or the review mode would apply it and the changeset would pass the circuit breaker (reviewModes.floors).
The op would wait for review and the space already has limits.pendingOpsPerSpace pending ops that wait on the owner's decision (spot checks and ops waiting for their verification not counted).
The title or text reads as a tool probe (test, probe, TEST_WRITE_CHECK). The message says the tool works and not to retry.

A decide, a revert, an entry's Reject or Confirm, a reopening of verifications, a change of the review mode or of automaticSpotChecks, or any request of the plan's on the user door (plan.who.owner) arrived with a session header, whatever the session's role: each is the owner's, on the user door, with no acting session.
A maintenance-only route was called by a session that is not a maintenance run of that space.
The calling session verifies, forems or judges work (task.verifiesTaskId, task.isForeman, a judgment session). Knowledge is not evidence, so such a session neither reads nor proposes.
An idempotency key the owner already used arrived with a different request (its normalized digest differs). The same request under the same key is a replay and gets the recorded answer.

A succeeded run asked to advance the cursor to a token behind the space's watermark: another run already went further, and the cursor only moves forward (maintenance.cursor.advance). The answer carries the cursor as it stands.
A cursor token that no dossier page of this space handed out: one that does not decode, one of another space, or a position past the furthest page the space's dossier route has issued.

An article write named an entry-set fingerprint that is not its topic's current one: the topic's entries changed while the articles were being written (articles.regeneration). Nothing is written; the next run writes them from the entries as they stand.

This account's pipeline is executed by the server (jobs.executor: ORBIT_WIKI_EXECUTOR=server, or canary with the account on its list): the runner door no longer hands a session that pipeline's material, nor accepts what a session's own model wrote for it — the wiki worker runs it with the System model, so no session's provider is asked. Nothing is read or written. Under the default runner nothing answers it.

A plan draft, an owner's edit of the plan, a proposed change to it or the acceptance of one did not pass the plan's gate (plan.gate): errors[] lists everything it found, each with its check and where it is. Nothing is stored.

A plan request was built on a version that is no longer the space's newest (plan.versions), confirmed a version that is no longer a draft, or answered a proposal already decided. Nothing is written; read the plan again.
A space's documents were to be written, or a change proposed to its plan, and the space has no plan its owner confirmed (plan.guard).

A maintenance run asked for, or reported on, a job of the space's plan, and its task was made for none, or the job has ended — its run said how, or its task ended first (plan.jobs.who.runner). Nothing is written.

A document write does not have the shape docs.schema gives it: a field it does not name, a repository footnote with no sha or no lines, a record footnote with no id, a section the confirmed plan's document does not have, a via entry that is not an entry of the space. errors[] lists everything it found, each { path, message }, the first docs.rules.errorsMax. Nothing is written.

refusalRules.orderNote: The order each op is checked in (design section 4.1); redaction, taint, effect and similar refuse nothing, they mark the op. changesetSize is limits.opsPerChangeset, read off the op's position alone. quota comes after the effect because what it counts depends on it: the review queue, the ops that wait (limitNotes.quota), and the circuit breaker, which counts what the review mode applies.
refusalRules.perOp: Each op is judged on its own. The ops that pass are recorded in one transaction; a refused op writes nothing.
refusalRules.status: A request none of whose ops was recorded answers with the HTTP status of its first refusal and every op's outcome in the body. A request that recorded something answers 200.
refusalRules.dryRun: Checks every op and answers as the request would, recording nothing and publishing nothing: every op's outcome, under the status the request would be answered with (status) — 200 when an op would be recorded, and the first refusal's otherwise. Its answer also carries breaker: the circuit breaker as the request found it, before any of its ops — {scope, activeAtStart, changed, remaining}: scope run for a maintenance run's changeset (maintenance.job.breaker) and changeset otherwise, activeAtStart the active entries it is counted against, changed the entries already changed through the review mode, and remaining how many more distinct entries the mode may change before an op is refused, null where no op is held to the breaker (a Manual space, the owner's own write, a space holding fewer than reviewModes.rules.breakerMinActiveEntries active entries). A request of the same ops recorded now refuses exactly the ones past remaining.
refusalRules.idempotency: An idempotency key is the owner's: the same key with the same normalized request returns the recorded answer, marked replayed, and writes and publishes nothing.
refusalRules.notFound: Another owner's space, entry or changeset is a plain 404 with no wiki code, the same answer as one that does not exist.
refusalRules.serviceToken: A service token is refused on both doors (403), as session_search refuses it: entries derive from conversation text on other machines.

agentSurface.why: An agent reads the wiki and proposes to it; it never decides. Three tools, split by risk rather than by entity.

wiki_search.returns: entries only: id, kind, title, summary, trust, anchorState, match (searchMatches) and score

wiki_get.returns: whole entries; each anchor with its last check (the ref and the time); each source with its orbit-* link

wiki_propose.returns: per op: pending (with waitsFor verification when an automatic space's verification, not the owner, decides it), applied, conflict (current revision and diff) or refused (reasons); similar[] beside an add or supersede

agentSurface.notTools: No tool accepts, confirms, decides, hard-deletes or overwrites a page. Confirmation exists only on the owner channel.
agentSurface.proposeDescription: Record only what someone could not read from the code: a decision and what was rejected, a pitfall and its fix, a convention. Cite the turns or records it came from; a claim you cannot cite is not ready. What you propose waits for the owner's review — do not tell the user it is saved.

runner.guard: RunnerAuthGuard, plus the calling session (X-Orbit-Session-Id) checked the way runner-watches.controller.ts checks it
runner.maintenanceNote: phase 2; any other session is refused WIKI_NOT_MAINTENANCE_SESSION. The maintenance job's check (maintenance.job.check) also answers the space's owner's runner with no session, since a task's acceptance command runs with none.
runner.verificationNote: The session that proposed the ops, and no other (reviewModes.verification.who.runner): X-Orbit-Session-Id is required, and another session's op or another owner's anything is a 404.
runner.importNote: phase 2 (import): orbit wiki import's two routes, for a session of the space's owner — X-Orbit-Session-Id is required, and another owner's space is a 404. When the server reads the account's imports, notes takes only readBy server and imports is refused WIKI_SERVER_EXECUTES (import.server.door).
runner.importJobNote: server execution, P5 (import.server): which path an import takes, the notes handed to an import job, and the job read back — for a session of the space's owner, X-Orbit-Session-Id required, another owner's space or job a 404.

verify.serverExecution: Under jobs.executor=server — or canary, for an account its list names — the server verifies what a session proposed and the session runs nothing: an op the space's Automatic mode holds back (reviewModes.verification.waits) is queued as a verify job for the session that proposed it the moment it is recorded (jobs.kindRuns.verify, jobs.make), the wiki worker asks the System model through the queue instead of a clean Claude Code in the session, and each verdict is reported through the same writer (reviewModes.verification.who.server) with the same prompt and the same strict reading this entry describes. This command is then no longer something a session has to run, and its meaning becomes "ask the server to verify these ops and wait for the result": the runner-side half of that — the command asking the server and waiting rather than running a model of its own — ships with the next runner release (P3, project 34bmzOkov3xN2yLPrnsCk). Until that release, and under the default jobs.executor=runner, nothing about this command changes: it reads the list, runs its clean Claude Code and reports, exactly as the rest of this entry says. A maintenance run is not a session either: it verifies its own ops in its own process, on the runner until P8 moves it.
verify.tool: none: a CLI verb with no MCP tool beside it. It runs a model, which is a runner's work rather than a tool call's, and it reports only what that model said.
verify.precondition: Verify only the ops this session proposed into an automatic space, and never write a verdict yourself: each verdict is the local model's, read from a separate clean call against the op's own sources, and a verdict that cannot be read is reported as nothing.
verify.does: Reads reviewModes.verification.list for --space, asks a clean Claude Code for one verdict per op, and reports each (reviewModes.verification.report) as soon as it has it, so what one run verified survives a run that stops half way. An op whose sources the list says are unreadable is asked about all the same: the server caps what its verdict can do (reviewModes.verification.evidence), and a duplicate still adds its sources. It stops at once on a 401 from the model's endpoint, and on a space that is no longer automatic.
verify.cleanClaudeCode: claude -p --bare --tools "" --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --no-session-persistence --output-format json --model <model> --system-prompt <the verifier's own, short> --settings <file naming an apiKeyHelper>, run with an empty HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and an environment built from an allowlist: none of the session's ORBIT_* variables, none of its own Claude Code's (of CLAUDE_CODE_* only the provider's CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS passes), and no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
verify.thinking: Off unless asked for: the clean call runs with CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=unset and MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0, so its request names no effort and no thinking, whatever effort the session's provider declares. --effort <low|medium|high|xhigh|max> asks for that effort instead (CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=<level>), and for thinking with it.
verify.model: The model and the endpoint are the ones the session's provider injected: ANTHROPIC_MODEL and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (--model names another model). The token is ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, read by the apiKeyHelper, because a bare run sends ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as x-api-key, which the local vLLM refuses 401, and ignores ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN.
verify.prompt: Hand-written, one op at a time: the entry's kind, title, summary and fields, the text of each source, and the neighbours a duplicate may name — each by a number of its own, E1 to En in the order listed, and never by its id: a local model copies a 21-character id wrong (09-30 to 10-02, 34XhYj76NhjjOJTEFEtFE came back as 34XhYj76NhjjOJTEFE run after run, and its op never got a verdict). The answer is one JSON object: {"verdict": one of reviewModes.verification.verdicts, "reason": one sentence, "duplicateOf": the number of the neighbour it duplicates, for a duplicate}, and the command reports the id that number stands for (reviewModes.verification.report). The object is read as encoding/json reads a struct: the keys in any case — {"Verdict": …, "Reason": …} names verdict and reason — and the reason's leading and trailing spaces trimmed as Go's strings.TrimSpace trims them (U+0085 among them).
verify.unreadable: An answer that is not that object — no JSON, another verdict, no reason, a duplicate naming no listed neighbour by its number — is not a verdict: nothing is reported for its op, which keeps waiting, and it counts as a failure. A number is one the prompt listed, exactly: an id, whole or cut short, is none, and nothing is guessed from a prefix; the verdict and the number are read as plan.gate.values reads a closed-set value. The command exits non-zero when any op failed. A maintenance run does not go by that exit: it verifies its own ops in its own process, asks once more about those left without a verdict, and what is still without one fails nothing (maintenance.job.run.steps, verify).

decide.sessionHeader: refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY whatever the session's role (the precedent is refuseSessionAuthoredConfirmation in coordinator-authority.ts)
decide.why: The confirmation card in the runner is not a gate: the server never checks it and a headless call passes it. So only the owner channel decides.

agentSurface.readBoundary: A session reads a space's entries only when its workspace is bound to that space: binding a workspace is the owner agreeing to share confirmed entries across the space's workspaces. A pending proposal is visible only to the session that made it.
agentSurface.excludedSessions: Verifier, foreman and judgment sessions are refused every wiki_* call (WIKI_SESSION_EXCLUDED) and are never pushed to.

rollout.canary: only the accounts ORBIT_WIKI_CANARY_OWNERS lists (comma-separated ids) have the wiki; every other account is as under off
rollout.off: the apiserver answers 404 WIKI_DISABLED on every route of both doors, the claim carries wikiDisabled, the runner mounts none of the three tools, no <orbit_wiki_context> is pushed, and an orbit-wiki: link card reads as unavailable

agentSurface.doorMissing: A runner newer than its apiserver says in a sentence that the server has no wiki door yet, as watch_tools.go's watchDoorMissing does.

realtime.scope: the space's owner, on the user-scoped control-plane stream (GET /api/events). The envelope names no session.
realtime.id: the space whose entries, review queue, bindings, settings, articles or plan changed
realtime.redaction: The space's id and nothing else: no entry, title, status, op or count. A client re-reads what it shows, and that read decides what it may see.
publishedWhen: a changeset recorded something, after its transaction commits
the owner decided ops, after the transaction commits
a space was created, its settings changed, or a workspace was bound
the owner reverted a changeset or rejected an entry, after the transaction commits
a verdict was recorded, after its transaction commits
pending ops expired or were withdrawn
a topic's articles were written, or a space's topics seeded, after the transaction commits
